parole.significato: A composition in Hindustani classical music.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindi बंदिश (bandiś, “binding”) from Classical Persian بندش (bandiš, “binding”).

parole.significato: A system of forced labour in parts of India.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindi बेगार (begār, “forced labor”), from Classical Persian بیگار (bē-gār).

parole.significato: A grandmother.
parole.testo: From Hindi बीबी (bībī), from Classical Persian بیبی (bī-bī).

parole.significato: A port or haven.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindi बंदर (bandar), from Classical Persian بندر (bandar).

parole.significato: An advance paid to a craftsman, a weaver, etc. by a trader in the goods produced.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindi दादनी (dādnī), from Classical Persian دَادَن (dādan).

parole.significato: A holder of any of various offices in various (usually Islamic) countries, usually some sort of councillor.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindi दीवान (dīvān), from Classical Persian دیوَان (dēwān), from Middle Persian dywʾn' (dēwān). Doublet of divan and douane.

parole.significato: A large iron pot, used in the army.
parole.testo: From Hindi देगची (degcī, “a kettle, a metallic cooking pot”), from Classical Persian دیگچه (degča, “a pot, small cauldron”), from دیگ (deg, “pot”) + ـچه (-ča).

parole.significato: A one-stringed musical instrument from India.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindi एकतारा (ektārā, literally “one-string”), ultimately from Classical Persian یکتار. Related to sitar.

parole.significato: Synonym of kiang.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindi गोरखर (gorkhar), from Classical Persian گورخر (gōrxar).

parole.significato: In or relating to the Hindi language.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindi हिंदी (hindī), from Classical Persian هِنْدِی (hindī). By surface analysis, Hind + -i. Distant doublet of Sindhi.

parole.significato: An infantryman; a soldier.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindustani جوان (jvān) / जवान (javān), from Classical Persian جوان (jawān, “young, a youth”).

parole.significato: An Indian worker at a port or dockyard, traditionally employed in pulling vessels out of the water for maintenance and…
parole.testo: From Hindi ख़लासी (xalāsī), from Classical Persian خلاصی (xalāsī).

parole.significato: A finely milled, refined and bleached wheat flour, used in making Indian foods such as samosa, chakli and bhatoora.
parole.testo: From Hindi मैदा (maidā), from Classical Persian مَیْدَه (mayda).

parole.significato: A servant, whether domestic, military, or civil.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindi नौकर (naukar), from Classical Persian نَوْکَر (nawkar), from Turkic (compare Chagatai نوکر (nökär), Ottoman Turkish نوكر (nöker), Azerbaijani nökər etc.), from Middle Mongol ᠨᠥᠬᠦᠷ (ṅwykwr /⁠nökör⁠/).

parole.significato: An Indian cavalry regiment.
parole.testo: From Hindi रिसाला (risālā), from Classical Persian رساله (risāla), from Arabic رِسَالَة (risāla)

parole.significato: Any green vegetable.
parole.testo: From Hindi सब्ज़ी (sabzī), from Classical Persian سبزی (sabzī).

parole.significato: An exclamation of praise for an achievement.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindi शाबाश (śābāś), from Classical Persian شاباش (šābāš), from the term شاد باش (šād bāš, “be happy”), from شاد (“joyful”) + باش (“be (imperative)”).

parole.significato: A hunting-ground, or enclosed preserve.
parole.testo: From Hindi शिकारगाह (śikārgāh), from Classical Persian شِکَارْگَاه (šikārgāh).

parole.significato: A soldier on horseback, especially one during the British Raj.
parole.testo: From Hindi/Urdu सवार (savār)/سوار (savār), from Classical Persian سوار (sawār, “horseman”).

parole.significato: stable or shed (for horses, cows, etc.)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindi तबेला (tabelā), from Classical Persian طَوِیلَه (tawīla), from Arabic طَوِيلَة (ṭawīla).

parole.significato: A cannon (weapon).
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindi तोप (top), which in turn is borrowed from Classical Persian توپ (tōp). Ultimately loaned from a Turkic word, which is derived from Proto-Turkic *top. Compare Turkish top.
